designs.title: Fanad Head Lighthouse
designs.why: Classic, giftable travel-poster format with a strong arched slab headline and accurate facts (first lit 1817, 1886 tower, 22 m). But the tower is thin and small against a very dark, busy cliff-and-surf lower half, so from 3 m the poster reads as a black mass with a title. Up close the line work looks auto-traced (blobby outlines), not engraved, and IRELAND appears twice.
designs.fix: Make the lighthouse bigger and more central, and open up the dense foreground rocks and sea with more white so the tower is the clear hero.

designs.title: Portland Head Light
designs.why: The strongest seller: an iconic, instantly recognizable view (tower, keeper's house, rocky ledges), a balanced composition, a confident headline and correct details (1787-1790, first lit 10 January 1791). It reads well on both tees. Small minus: the rock foreground is heavy and the line work is slightly traced and blotchy at full size.
designs.fix: Lighten the bottom third of the rocks so the house and tower carry the image and the print isn't a heavy ink slab on the chest.

designs.title: Cape Agulhas Lighthouse
designs.why: The banded tower is a great graphic hook and the headline is the cleanest of the four. But the side panel is thin (just two dates and the coordinates), there is no LIGHTHOUSE subline, so the header feels unfinished next to the others, and the keeper's buildings read as generic cottages. The vegetation foreground is dense and muddy.
designs.fix: Add a subline under the title (e.g. LIGHTHOUSE / Southernmost tip of Africa) and a line or two on the left panel to give the header the same finish as the rest of the series.

designs.title: Phare de Saint-Mathieu
designs.why: The abbey ruins beside the tower give it the most distinctive story and silhouette in the set. The two-tier French headline with its PLOUGONVELIN - FINISTERE - BRETAGNE line feels authentic, and the facts are right (1835, 37 m). The weak spots: the big SAINT-MATHIEU line crowds the frame edges, and the lower half is again a dense dark mass with traced-looking edges.
designs.fix: Shrink the SAINT-MATHIEU line slightly to give it side margin, and thin out the foreground cliff texture so the ruins and tower stand out.
